comments.author: @jaimerubio4255
comments.text:
Even though we are considered as U.S.A. citizens since 1917 we cannot vote in the U.S.A. elections. We have been a colony of the U.S.A. after we were invaded by the U.S.A. on July 25, 1898. Then the U.S.A. came up with the Merchant Marine Act (Jones Act) in 1920, a ferderal cabotage law which mandates that all maritime cargo transported between U.S.A. ports (including between the U.S.A. and Puerto Rico) must be carried on ships that are U.S.A.- built, U.S.A.-owned, U.S.A.-flagged, and crewed by U.S.A. citizens.
Great business for the U.S.A., bad business for the Puerto Ricans which end up paying more because shipments have to go through the U.S.A. first before getting to Puerto Rico.
